- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or use moving average to smooth.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) periods, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent history shows mean reversion toward prior 5–7 day average.
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is rising, assume momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is rising or volatility is increasing.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive sentiment >0.6), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
